title: Stall judge falls back to a discovered tiny model that cannot produce verdicts
description:
With no pinned `interventions.judge_model`, `judgeModel` (internal/core/judge.go:131) falls back to the cheapest catalog model. Since Ramp model discovery, that is a discovered tiny model (ramp/nemotron-lightning-3p5-30b-a3b), which returned "unparseable verdict" 22 of 24 times in worker session ae7e6873 (2026-10-02). The stall judge was effectively disabled; no_progress_turns climbed to 26 with no real judgment.

Fix: exclude `Discovered` models from the fallback (prefer curated efficient-tier models). Optionally, when the verdict is unparseable and Jev is configured, use the Jev stall_judge answer instead of treating it as no-intervene. Add a test that the fallback skips discovered models.

title: False review-remediation stall: turn counter accumulates across review cycles
description:
`progressTracker.reviewRemediationTurns` (internal/core/progress.go) counts turns spent with `fixPending` after a failed independent review, but it is only reset by `resetStall` (an escalation) and when `markReviewRejected` first enters remediation. It never resets when a fix lands or when a later review rejects the next diff, so turns accumulate across every review cycle in a run.

Once the total reaches 8, `reviewRemediationReason` reports "agent spent eight turns after a failed independent review without fixing anything" and the escalation ladder climbs, even though the agent fixed each finding.

Observed in session ee571636 (2026-10-04, adding five Ramp models to the catalog): four reviews each rejected the change for a distinct real bug and the agent fixed each one, yet false escalations fired at 16:07:57 (rung 1, nudge telling it to take a "materially different approach") and 16:14:31 (rung 2, forced model switch). Two more false trips would compact/restate and then pause the run to ask the person.

Fix: reset `reviewRemediationTurns` in `markReviewRejected` on every rejection, so it measures turns since the latest rejection without an edit. Add a test covering several reject→fix cycles that each take a few turns.

title: Output cap resets to 8K every turn after a truncation retry
description:
When a response is cut off at the output limit with only reasoning, the engine doubles `outputCap` and retries (internal/core/engine.go ~1081), but `outputCap` is reset to `defaultOutputCap` at the next turn (engine.go:1202). A model that needs more room for reasoning therefore burns the full 8K cap on nothing at the start of every hard turn.

Observed in worker session ae7e6873 (2026-10-02, ramp/claude-sonnet-5): 13 truncated reasoning-only responses at 8K, each about 76s and $0.14, each followed by a successful 16K retry. Roughly $1.90 and 15 minutes wasted.

Fix: keep the raised cap for the rest of the session, per model, rather than resetting each turn. Keep the maxOutputCap bound. Add a test that a second turn after a truncation starts at the raised cap.

title: Agent self-reviews before submitting, duplicating the harness independent review
description:
In session ee571636 (2026-10-04), the agent spawned its own review worker (7b6eb9ef, $0.53, ~1.5 min) on its diff before submitting; the harness then ran its own independent review (ae7d90d2) on the same diff.

Options: (a) tell the prompt that Orrery reviews completed changes independently, so the agent should not spawn a review worker for its own diff; or (b) let the harness skip its review when an agent-spawned review with review=true already passed on the same diff hash (reviewDiffHash). (a) is cheaper and simpler; (b) keeps the work if the agent does it anyway.
